Applying in Brooklyn: the short version

  • Who qualifies: pregnant and postpartum women, infants, and children under 5 — applied for by any caregiver, including dads and grandparents. Full rules.
  • Income: up to $61,050/year for a family of 4 (2026-2027 table), or automatic with Medicaid/SNAP/TANF. Full table.
  • What you get: monthly foods on an eWIC card, infant formula covered in full, produce dollars, and breastfeeding support. Details.

Frequently asked questions

What are the WIC income limits in Brooklyn?

New York uses the federal maximum: 185% of poverty. For July 2026-June 2027 that's $40,034/year for a household of 2, $50,542 for 3, $61,050 for 4 — and a pregnancy counts as an extra member. Medicaid, SNAP or TANF enrollment qualifies you automatically regardless of income.

How do I apply for WIC in Brooklyn?

Call one of the clinics above to book a certification appointment. Bring photo ID, proof of address, proof of income (or your Medicaid/SNAP card) and the children applying. Most families leave the first visit certified, with the eWIC card in hand.

Can I get WIC while pregnant with no other kids?

Yes — pregnancy alone qualifies as a category from the moment it's confirmed, and you count as a household of at least 2 for income. Pregnant applicants also get priority scheduling.
